Question 1 of 20, Level 1

1MCQPYQ-style1 mark
If AAA is a matrix of order m×nm \times nm×n and BBB is a matrix such that AB′AB'AB′ and B′AB'AB′A are both defined, then the order of BBB is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Pa×b Qc×dP_{a \times b}\,Q_{c \times d}Pa×b​Qc×d​ is defined only if b=cb = cb=c.

  1. 1

    Let BBB be of order u×vu \times vu×v, so B′B'B′ is v×uv \times uv×u.

  2. 2

    Am×nBv×u′A_{m \times n}B'_{v \times u}Am×n​Bv×u′​ is defined.

    n=vn = vn=v
  3. 3

    Bv×u′Am×nB'_{v \times u}A_{m \times n}Bv×u′​Am×n​ is defined.

    u=mu = mu=m
  4. 4

    So BBB has order u×v=m×nu \times v = m \times nu×v=m×n. Option (D).

    1
Answer(D) m×n\displaystyle m \times nm×n

Watch out Finding the order of B′B'B′ (n×mn \times mn×m) and forgetting to transpose back to BBB.

Question 2 of 20, Level 1

2MCQPYQ-style1 mark
If [x+y25xy]=[6258]\begin{bmatrix} x + y & 2 \\ 5 & xy \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 2 \\ 5 & 8 \end{bmatrix}[x+y5​2xy​]=[65​28​], then the value of (24x+24y)\left(\dfrac{24}{x} + \dfrac{24}{y}\right)(x24​+y24​) is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Equal matrices have equal corresponding elements.

  1. 1

    Equate corresponding elements.

    x+y=6,xy=8x + y = 6, \qquad xy = 8x+y=6,xy=8
  2. 2

    Take 24 common and use a common denominator.

    24x+24y=24(x+y)xy=24×68=18\dfrac{24}{x} + \dfrac{24}{y} = \dfrac{24(x + y)}{xy} = \dfrac{24 \times 6}{8} = 18x24​+y24​=xy24(x+y)​=824×6​=1824x+24y=24(x+y)xy=24×68=18\displaystyle \dfrac{24}{x} + \dfrac{24}{y} = \dfrac{24(x + y)}{xy} = \dfrac{24 \times 6}{8} = 18x24​+y24​=xy24(x+y)​=824×6​=18
    1
  3. 3

    Hence option (D).

Answer(D) 18\displaystyle 1818

Watch out Writing 24x+24y=24x+y=4\dfrac{24}{x} + \dfrac{24}{y} = \dfrac{24}{x + y} = 4x24​+y24​=x+y24​=4; fractions do not add like that.

Question 1Question 3

Question 3 of 20, Level 1

3MCQNCERT Ex 3.3 Q111 mark
If AAA and BBB are symmetric matrices of the same order, then AB−BAAB - BAAB−BA is a:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea (AB)′=B′A′(AB)' = B'A'(AB)′=B′A′; symmetric means A′=AA' = AA′=A.

  1. 1

    Take the transpose of AB−BAAB - BAAB−BA.

    (AB−BA)′=(AB)′−(BA)′=B′A′−A′B′(AB - BA)' = (AB)' - (BA)' = B'A' - A'B'(AB−BA)′=(AB)′−(BA)′=B′A′−A′B′(AB−BA)′=(AB)′−(BA)′=B′A′−A′B′\displaystyle (AB - BA)' = (AB)' - (BA)' = B'A' - A'B'(AB−BA)′=(AB)′−(BA)′=B′A′−A′B′
  2. 2

    Use A′=AA' = AA′=A and B′=BB' = BB′=B.

    (AB−BA)′=BA−AB=−(AB−BA)(AB - BA)' = BA - AB = -(AB - BA)(AB−BA)′=BA−AB=−(AB−BA)
    1
  3. 3

    So AB−BAAB - BAAB−BA is skew-symmetric. Option (A).

Answer(A) skew-symmetric matrix

Watch out Writing (AB)′=A′B′(AB)' = A'B'(AB)′=A′B′ and concluding the matrix is symmetric.

Let A=[aij]A = [a_{ij}]A=[aij​] be a 3×23 \times 23×2 matrix whose elements are given by aij=(i−3j)2a_{ij} = (i - 3j)^2aij​=(i−3j)2. The element in the 2nd row and 3rd column of A′A'A′ is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea The (i,j)(i, j)(i,j) element of A′A'A′ is the (j,i)(j, i)(j,i) element of AAA.

  1. 1

    AAA is 3×23 \times 23×2, so A′A'A′ is 2×32 \times 32×3 and has a (2,3)(2, 3)(2,3) element.

  2. 2

    Swap the indices.

    (A′)23=a32(A')_{23} = a_{32}(A′)23​=a32​
  3. 3

    Put i=3i = 3i=3, j=2j = 2j=2 in the rule.

    a32=(3−6)2=9a_{32} = (3 - 6)^2 = 9a32​=(3−6)2=9
    1
  4. 4

    Hence option (B).

Answer(B) 9\displaystyle 99

Watch out Putting i=2i = 2i=2, j=3j = 3j=3 in the rule to get 494949; a23a_{23}a23​ does not even exist in AAA.

Question 3Question 5

Question 5 of 20, Level 1

5MCQNCERT Exemplar1 mark
If AAA is a square matrix such that A2=IA^2 = IA2=I, then (A−I)3+(A+I)3−7A(A - I)^3 + (A + I)^3 - 7A(A−I)3+(A+I)3−7A is equal to:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea AAA and III commute, so the binomial expansion holds; A3=A⋅A2=AA^3 = A \cdot A^2 = AA3=A⋅A2=A.

  1. 1

    Expand both cubes.

    (A−I)3=A3−3A2+3A−I(A+I)3=A3+3A2+3A+I\begin{aligned} (A - I)^3 &= A^3 - 3A^2 + 3A - I \\ (A + I)^3 &= A^3 + 3A^2 + 3A + I \end{aligned}(A−I)3(A+I)3​=A3−3A2+3A−I=A3+3A2+3A+I​
  2. 2

    Add; the A2A^2A2 and III terms cancel.

    (A−I)3+(A+I)3=2A3+6A(A - I)^3 + (A + I)^3 = 2A^3 + 6A(A−I)3+(A+I)3=2A3+6A
  3. 3

    Use A3=A⋅A2=A⋅I=AA^3 = A \cdot A^2 = A \cdot I = AA3=A⋅A2=A⋅I=A.

    2A+6A−7A=A2A + 6A - 7A = A2A+6A−7A=A
    1
  4. 4

    Hence option (A).

Answer(A) A\displaystyle AA

Watch out Putting A3=IA^3 = IA3=I; with A2=IA^2 = IA2=I we get A3=AA^3 = AA3=A.

Assertion (A): For A=[2−41−2]A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}A=[21​−4−2​], A2=OA^2 = OA2=O. Reason (R): If the product of two matrices is a zero matrix, then at least one of the two matrices must be a zero matrix.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Two non-zero matrices can have a zero product.

  1. 1

    Find A2A^2A2.

    A2=[4−4−8+82−2−4+4]=[0000]A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 4 - 4 & -8 + 8 \\ 2 - 2 & -4 + 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}A2=[4−42−2​−8+8−4+4​]=[00​00​]
  2. 2

    So Assertion (A) is true.

  3. 3

    Here A⋅A=OA \cdot A = OA⋅A=O but A≠OA \ne OA=O, so Reason (R) is false.

  4. 4

    Hence option (C).

    1
Answer(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

Watch out Carrying the rule "ab=0⇒a=0ab = 0 \Rightarrow a = 0ab=0⇒a=0 or b=0b = 0b=0" from numbers over to matrices.

Find the values of xxx and yyy if 2[x3yx]−[1yx4]=[5252]2\begin{bmatrix} x & 3 \\ y & x \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 1 & y \\ x & 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 \end{bmatrix}2[xy​3x​]−[1x​y4​]=[55​22​].

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

  1. 1

    Multiply by 2 and subtract.

    [2x−16−y2y−x2x−4]=[5252]\begin{bmatrix} 2x - 1 & 6 - y \\ 2y - x & 2x - 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 \end{bmatrix}[2x−12y−x​6−y2x−4​]=[55​22​]
    ½
  2. 2

    Equate the (1,1)(1,1)(1,1) elements.

    2x−1=5  ⇒  x=32x - 1 = 5 \;\Rightarrow\; x = 32x−1=5⇒x=3
    ½
  3. 3

    Equate the (1,2)(1,2)(1,2) elements.

    6−y=2  ⇒  y=46 - y = 2 \;\Rightarrow\; y = 46−y=2⇒y=4
    ½
  4. 4

    Check the other two elements.

    2y−x=8−3=5,2x−4=6−4=22y - x = 8 - 3 = 5, \qquad 2x - 4 = 6 - 4 = 22y−x=8−3=5,2x−4=6−4=22y−x=8−3=5,2x−4=6−4=2\displaystyle 2y - x = 8 - 3 = 5, \qquad 2x - 4 = 6 - 4 = 22y−x=8−3=5,2x−4=6−4=2
    ½
  5. 5

    Hence x=3x = 3x=3 and y=4y = 4y=4.

Answerx=3\displaystyle x = 3x=3, y=4\displaystyle y = 4y=4

Watch out Multiplying only the first row by 2 instead of every element.

    a31=3−1=2,a32=3−2=1,a33=0a_{31} = 3 - 1 = 2,\quad a_{32} = 3 - 2 = 1,\quad a_{33} = 0a31​=3−1=2,a32​=3−2=1,a33​=0a31=3−1=2,a32=3−2=1,a33=0\displaystyle a_{31} = 3 - 1 = 2,\quad a_{32} = 3 - 2 = 1,\quad a_{33} = 0a31​=3−1=2,a32​=3−2=1,a33​=0
    ½
  4. 4

    A=[034105210]A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}A=​012​301​450​​

For the matrix A=[3211]A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}A=[31​21​], find the numbers aaa and bbb such that A2+aA+bI=OA^2 + aA + bI = OA2+aA+bI=O. Hence find A−1A^{-1}A−1.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

  1. 1

    Find A2A^2A2.

    A2=[9+26+23+12+1]=[11843]A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 9 + 2 & 6 + 2 \\ 3 + 1 & 2 + 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 11 & 8 \\ 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix}A2=[9+23+1​6+22+1​]=[114​83​]
    1
  2. 2

    Write A2+aA+bIA^2 + aA + bIA2+aA+bI and set it equal to OOO.

    [11+3a+b8+2a4+a3+a+b]=[0000]\begin{bmatrix} 11 + 3a + b & 8 + 2a \\ 4 + a & 3 + a + b \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}[11+3a+b4+a​8+2a3+a+b​]=[00​00​]
    ½
  3. 3

    From 4+a=04 + a = 04+a=0 and 3+a+b=03 + a + b = 03+a+b=0.

    a=−4,b=1a = -4, \qquad b = 1a=−4,b=1

    These also satisfy 11+3a+b=011 + 3a + b = 011+3a+b=0 and 8+2a=08 + 2a = 08+2a=0.

    ½
  4. 4

    So A2−4A+I=OA^2 - 4A + I = OA2−4A+I=O. Rearrange and take AAA common.

    A(4I−A)=I  ⇒  A−1=4I−AA(4I - A) = I \;\Rightarrow\; A^{-1} = 4I - AA(4I−A)=I⇒A−1=4I−AA(4I−A)=I  ⇒  A−1=4I−A\displaystyle A(4I - A) = I \;\Rightarrow\; A^{-1} = 4I - AA(4I−A)=I⇒A−1=4I−A

    Also (4I−A)A=I(4I - A)A = I(4I−A)A=I.

    ½
  5. 5

    Compute 4I−A4I - A4I−A.

    A−1=[4−3−2−14−1]=[1−2−13]A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 - 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 4 - 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}A−1=[4−3−1​−24−1​]=[1−1​−23​]
    ½
Answera=−4\displaystyle a = -4a=−4, b=1\displaystyle b = 1b=1; A−1=[1−2−13]\displaystyle A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}A−1=[1−1​−23​]

Express the matrix A=[25−31467−20]A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & 4 & 6 \\ 7 & -2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}A=​217​54−2​−360​​ as the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea A=12(A+A′)+12(A−A′)A = \tfrac{1}{2}(A + A') + \tfrac{1}{2}(A - A')A=21​(A+A′)+21​(A−A′): symmetric part plus skew-symmetric part.

  1. 1

    Write the transpose.

    A′=[21754−2−360]A' = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 7 \\ 5 & 4 & -2 \\ -3 & 6 & 0 \end{bmatrix}A′=​25−3​146​7−20​​
    ½
  2. 2

    Symmetric part P=12(A+A′)P = \tfrac{1}{2}(A + A')P=21​(A+A′).

    P=12[464684440]=[232342220]P = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 6 & 4 \\ 6 & 8 & 4 \\ 4 & 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}P=21​​464​684​440​​=​232​342​220​​
    ½
  3. 3

    Check: P′=PP' = PP′=P, so PPP is symmetric.

    ½
  4. 4

    Skew-symmetric part Q=12(A−A′)Q = \tfrac{1}{2}(A - A')Q=21​(A−A′).

    Q=12[04−10−40810−80]=[02−5−2045−40]Q = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 4 & -10 \\ -4 & 0 & 8 \\ 10 & -8 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & -5 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ 5 & -4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}Q=21​​0−410​40−8​−1080​​=​0−25​20−4​−540​​
    ½
  5. 5

    Check: Q′=−QQ' = -QQ′=−Q, so QQQ is skew-symmetric.

    ½
  6. 6

    Add to verify: P+Q=AP + Q = AP+Q=A.

    [232342220]+[02−5−2045−40]=[25−31467−20]=A\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & -5 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ 5 & -4 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & 4 & 6 \\ 7 & -2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = A​232​342​220​​+​0−25​20−4​−540​​=​217​54−2​−360​​=A
    ½
AnswerA=[232342220]+[02−5−2045−40]\displaystyle A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & -5 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ 5 & -4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}A=​232​342​220​​+​0−25​20−4​−540​​

Watch out Sign slip in A−A′A - A'A−A′ at the (1,3)(1,3)(1,3) place: −3−7=−10-3 - 7 = -10−3−7=−10, not 444.

Find the matrices XXX and YYY if X+2Y=[47−45]X + 2Y = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 7 \\ -4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}X+2Y=[4−4​75​] and 2X−Y=[3−625]2X - Y = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -6 \\ 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}2X−Y=[32​−65​].

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Matrix equations are solved like simultaneous equations: eliminate one matrix.

  1. 1

    Multiply the second equation by 2 and add the first; YYY cancels.

    5X=[47−45]+[6−12410]=[10−5015]5X = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 7 \\ -4 & 5 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -12 \\ 4 & 10 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 15 \end{bmatrix}5X=[4−4​75​]+[64​−1210​]=[100​−515​]
    ½
  2. 2

    Divide by 5.

    X=[2−103]X = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}X=[20​−13​]
    ½
  3. 3

    From the second equation, Y=2X−[3−625]Y = 2X - \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -6 \\ 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}Y=2X−[32​−65​].

    Y=[4−206]−[3−625]Y = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -6 \\ 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}Y=[40​−26​]−[32​−65​]
    ½
  4. 4

    Subtract element by element.

    Y=[14−21]Y = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}Y=[1−2​41​]
    ½
AnswerX=[2−103]\displaystyle X = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}X=[20​−13​], Y=[14−21]\displaystyle Y = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}Y=[1−2​41​]

Watch out Sign slip in −2−(−6)=4-2 - (-6) = 4−2−(−6)=4 at the (1,2)(1,2)(1,2) place of YYY.

Question 10Question 12

Question 12 of 20, Level 2

12Short answerBoard-pattern3 marks
Find xxx, if [x1−1][120201102][xx2]=O\begin{bmatrix} x & 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ x \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} = O[x​1​−1​]​121​200​012​​​xx2​​=O.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea (1×3)(3×3)=1×3(1 \times 3)(3 \times 3) = 1 \times 3(1×3)(3×3)=1×3, then (1×3)(3×1)=1×1(1 \times 3)(3 \times 1) = 1 \times 1(1×3)(3×1)=1×1.

  1. 1

    Multiply the row matrix by the 3×33 \times 33×3 matrix.

    [x+2−12x+0+00+1−2]=[x+12x−1]\begin{bmatrix} x + 2 - 1 & 2x + 0 + 0 & 0 + 1 - 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} x + 1 & 2x & -1 \end{bmatrix}[x+2−1​2x+0+0​0+1−2​]=[x+1​2x​−1​]
    1
  2. 2

    Multiply by the column matrix.

    x(x+1)+x(2x)+2(−1)=3x2+x−2x(x + 1) + x(2x) + 2(-1) = 3x^2 + x - 2x(x+1)+x(2x)+2(−1)=3x2+x−2x(x+1)+x(2x)+2(−1)=3x2+x−2\displaystyle x(x + 1) + x(2x) + 2(-1) = 3x^2 + x - 2x(x+1)+x(2x)+2(−1)=3x2+x−2
    1
  3. 3

    Set the 1×11 \times 11×1 matrix equal to OOO and factorise.

    3x2+x−2=0  ⇒  (3x−2)(x+1)=03x^2 + x - 2 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; (3x - 2)(x + 1) = 03x2+x−2=0⇒(3x−2)(x+1)=03x2+x−2=0  ⇒  (3x−2)(x+1)=0\displaystyle 3x^2 + x - 2 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; (3x - 2)(x + 1) = 03x2+x−2=0⇒(3x−2)(x+1)=0

    Add them: RHS.

    pI+qA+rA2=[pqrprp+qrq+r2pq+pr2pr+q2+qr2p+2qr+r3]pI + qA + rA^2 = \begin{bmatrix} p & q & r \\ pr & p + qr & q + r^2 \\ pq + pr^2 & pr + q^2 + qr^2 & p + 2qr + r^3 \end{bmatrix}pI+qA+rA2=​pprpq+pr2​qp+qrpr+q2+qr2​rq+r2p+2qr+r3​​
    1
  5. 5

    LHS = RHS element by element.

    A3=pI+qA+rA2A^3 = pI + qA + rA^2A3=pI+qA+rA2
    ½
AnswerBoth sides equal [pqrprp+qrq+r2pq+pr2pr+q2+qr2p+2qr+r3]\displaystyle \begin{bmatrix} p & q & r \\ pr & p + qr & q + r^2 \\ pq + pr^2 & pr + q^2 + qr^2 & p + 2qr + r^3 \end{bmatrix}​pprpq+pr2​qp+qrpr+q2+qr2​rq+r2p+2qr+r3​​, so A3=pI+qA+rA2\displaystyle A^3 = pI + qA + rA^2A3=pI+qA+rA2.

Watch out Adding ppp to every element for pIpIpI; it adds ppp only on the diagonal.

Question 20 of 20, Level 3

20Case studyBoard-pattern4 marks
Case Study: A dairy cooperative sells milk, curd and paneer in two towns P and Q. In one week, town P buys 500 litres of milk, 150 kg of curd and 40 kg of paneer; town Q buys 400 litres of milk, 200 kg of curd and 50 kg of paneer. The selling prices are ₹60 per litre of milk, ₹80 per kg of curd and ₹400 per kg of paneer. The cost prices are ₹45, ₹60 and ₹320 respectively.
  1. (i)Write the weekly sales as a 2×32 \times 32×3 matrix and the selling prices as a column matrix.1 mark
  2. (ii)Find the revenue from town P.1 mark
  3. (iii)(a)Using matrix multiplication, find the profit from each town and the total profit.2 marks
  4. OR
  5. (iii)(b)The cooperative changes the price of paneer to ₹xxx per kg, keeping the other prices the same. The total revenue from both towns becomes ₹1,22,500. Using matrices, find xxx.2 marks

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

(i)1 mark

  1. 1

    Rows = towns P, Q; columns = milk, curd, paneer.

    S=[5001504040020050]S = \begin{bmatrix} 500 & 150 & 40 \\ 400 & 200 & 50 \end{bmatrix}S=[500400​150200​4050​]
    ½
  2. 2

    Selling prices as a column matrix.

    P=[6080400]P = \begin{bmatrix} 60 \\ 80 \\ 400 \end{bmatrix}P=​6080400​​
    ½
Answer (i)S=[5001504040020050]\displaystyle S = \begin{bmatrix} 500 & 150 & 40 \\ 400 & 200 & 50 \end{bmatrix}S=[500400​150200​4050​], P=[6080400]\displaystyle P = \begin{bmatrix} 60 \\ 80 \\ 400 \end{bmatrix}P=​6080400​​

(ii)1 mark

  1. 1

    Multiply town P's row by the price column.

    [50015040][6080400]=30000+12000+16000\begin{bmatrix} 500 & 150 & 40 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 60 \\ 80 \\ 400 \end{bmatrix} = 30000 + 12000 + 16000[500​150​40​]​6080400​​=30000+12000+16000
    ½
  2. 2

    Revenue from town P is ₹58,000.

    =58000= 58000=58000
    ½
Answer (ii)₹58,000

(iii)(a)2 marks

  1. 1

    Profit per unit = selling price −-− cost price.

    [6080400]−[4560320]=[152080]\begin{bmatrix} 60 \\ 80 \\ 400 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 45 \\ 60 \\ 320 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 15 \\ 20 \\ 80 \end{bmatrix}​6080400​​−​4560320​​=​152080​​
    ½
  2. 2

    Profit matrix = SSS times the profit column.

    [5001504040020050][152080]=[7500+3000+32006000+4000+4000]=[1370014000]\begin{bmatrix} 500 & 150 & 40 \\ 400 & 200 & 50 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 15 \\ 20 \\ 80 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 7500 + 3000 + 3200 \\ 6000 + 4000 + 4000 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 13700 \\ 14000 \end{bmatrix}[500400​150200​4050​]​152080​​=[7500+3000+32006000+4000+4000​]=[1370014000​]
    1
  3. 3

    Total profit =13700+14000=27700= 13700 + 14000 = 27700=13700+14000=27700.

    ½
Answer (iii)(a)Town P: ₹13,700; town Q: ₹14,000; total ₹27,700
OR

(iii)(b)2 marks

  1. 1

    New price column has xxx for paneer.

    [5001504040020050][6080x]=[42000+40x40000+50x]\begin{bmatrix} 500 & 150 & 40 \\ 400 & 200 & 50 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 60 \\ 80 \\ x \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 42000 + 40x \\ 40000 + 50x \end{bmatrix}[500400​150200​4050​]​6080x​​=[42000+40x40000+50x​]
    1
  2. 2

    Total revenue is ₹1,22,500.

    82000+90x=122500  ⇒  90x=4050082000 + 90x = 122500 \;\Rightarrow\; 90x = 4050082000+90x=122500⇒90x=4050082000+90x=122500  ⇒  90x=40500\displaystyle 82000 + 90x = 122500 \;\Rightarrow\; 90x = 4050082000+90x=122500⇒90x=40500
    ½
  3. 3

    Hence the new price of paneer.

    x=450x = 450x=450
    ½
Answer (iii)(b)x=450\displaystyle x = 450x=450, i.e. ₹450 per kg

Watch out Using the selling prices instead of (selling −-− cost) when finding profit.
